newsitem.title: CHINA: Human rights group says China dissident beaten.
newsitem.headline: Human rights group says China dissident beaten.

text.p: A human rights group said on Saturday that prominent Chinese dissident Yao Zhenxiang, were beaten while in detention and that he and his brother had been denied the right of appeal against their detention.

The New York-based Human Rights in China said in a statement faxed to Reuters that Yao Zhenxiang, had been "beaten severely" by Shanghai Public Security officials since being taken into custody in April.
Police and Yao's family could not be reached for comment.
The group said the brothers had been stripped of their right of appeal and had been denied the right to file a lawsuit against the government.
Yao Zhenxiang, a long-time financier of the struggling democracy movement in China, fled to Hong Kong in 1994 and was granted political asylum in France.
Human Rights in China has said Yao Zhenxiang, returned to Shanghai in February this year after the police promised not to arrest him.
